transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-17
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Northforge Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Northforge Security), Priya Patel (Northforge Legal), Jamal Reed (Northforge Infra)

Summary:
Quick procurement kickoff to align on sourcing pathway, KYC requirements, vendor DPA/MSA redlines, KMS/HSM integration, and SLA expectations. Customer wants clarity on private deployment options, key management, and billing approval path. Action items and pilot scope agreed.

Topics covered:
- MSA / DPA redline expectations and timeline
- SOC2 / ISO docs and KYC artifacts
- KMS / HSM integration options (bring-your-own vs managed)
- SSO / SAML and RBAC model for Redwood Console and Private installs
- SLA targets, uptime, latency SLOs, and escalation paths
- Pilot pricing and POC scope (2-week dedicated pilot)

Action items (recap):
(see action_items field above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for making time, i'll do a quick intro — maya from redwood, ae on the account, and diego our solutions engineer is here to go over the technical pieces. how's that sound?
[00:12] Aisha: hi, yes thanks — we wanted a single call to get procurement and security aligned early, so appreciate it. this is Aisha from procurement.
[00:18] Liam: morning, liam here, security architecture. we've got some KMS questions and also SOC2 artifacts to review.
[00:25] Priya: priya legal. we'll be looking at any dpa/msa exceptions. please note we have a standard list of clauses we ask vendors to accept.
[00:31] Maya: great, high level agenda: dpa/msad maybe i said msad, sorry, MSA/DPA timeline, artifacts (SOC2/ISO), KMS options — BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys, SSO and RBAC, and then pilot pricing and SLA targets. diego will jump in on the infra details.
[00:45] Diego: thanks, maya. quick note — on Redwood side we support hosted api, dedicated pools, and private vpc deployments. sometimes in call notes i see "Redwood Privates" spelled weirdly, lol, but the options are: hosted (fastest), dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc/on-prem). for keys we support external KMS connectors (aws kms, azure key vault, gcp kms) and also HSM-backed KMS via partners.
[01:12] Jamal: so for Northforge, we're focused on keys in our tenancy, not shared. if we do BYOK we need to be clear about session keys, rotation, and logs — also who's responsible for key compromise notifications.
[01:28] Diego: right, in BYOK mode you hold the CMK and we perform envelope encryption; logs show key use with request IDs. we can surface audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. note: some folks call KV cache "kv cash" in notes — that's unrelated but i keep an eye out for cache behavior during inference.
[01:50] Liam: okay, two things: 1) we need key rotation policy details, and 2) we want to confirm our RBAC model for the console and for API tokens — can we restrict model deployment & rollout permissions to certain groups?
[02:05] Diego: yes, our console supports role-based access. you can map SAML groups to roles (admin, ops, read-only). for API tokens, we recommend short-lived tokens and minting via your identity provider; we also provide token-level audit trails.
[02:22] Priya: on the DPA — our commercial team will want to add a clause about subprocessor notification windows and data residency. what's your standard for data deletion and retention for hosted inference?
[02:34] Maya: generally, hosted api has configurable retention — default is 30 days for logs and 0 retention for customer payload if requested. for Dedicated/Private footprints we can do no retention on our side and all telemetry goes to your logging endpoint. i'll share the exact data flow doc.
[02:50] Aisha: procurement and legal will need the SOC2 Type II report and any ISO attestations. do you have a recent report?
[02:58] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II report is available — i'll upload to the secure folder. ISO 27001 cert is included.
[03:05] Jamal: a practical item: for the pilot we want to run in our us-west region with direct vpc peering. will redwood support cross-account vpc peering or transit?
[03:17] Diego: we support VPC peering and private link style integrations depending on cloud. for a short pilot, peering + dedicated capacity should be easiest. we'll document the network ports and egress requirements.
[03:31] Liam: SLA stuff — we need 99.9% for production, but for pilot we can accept best-effort. what do your enterprise SLAs look like and how do you measure latency SLOs?
[03:40] Maya: enterprise SLA tiers include 99.9% uptime for Dedicated, with credits for breaches. latency SLOs are defined per model & route; our console shows token-level latency and p95/p99. we can pin a model variant for the pilot to ensure consistent latency.
[03:57] Priya: on indemnity/data clauses — we may propose standard vendor indemnity with carveouts for open models. also, we will review pricing model (per-token vs flat capacity) for budget.
[04:09] Aisha: budget timeline — procurement needs final pricing approved by 2025-05-02 to hit our Q2 commit.
[04:16] Maya: understood, we'll work to get pricing and the pilot scoping doc to you by next week.
[04:24] Diego: technical question from my side: do you plan to use large context windows? that'll affect memory and we can recommend quantization / batching profiles.
[04:33] Jamal: yes, some products will use 8k windows, others 32k. for the latter we'll likely need dedicated instances.
[04:40] Diego: good to know — for 32k we generally recommend dedicated reserved capacity and possible 4-bit quantization for cost savings, we can propose model variants.
[04:51] Liam: one more security: can you support customer-managed HSM with attestation that private keys never leave HSM?
[04:58] Diego: yes, through our HSM partner flows we can keep keys in customer HSM; we'll need a short architectural review to validate the attestation mechanism.
[05:10] Priya: can you clarify breach notification timelines? we usually ask for 72 hours.
[05:15] Maya: standard vendor timeline is 72 hours; we can confirm in the DPA.
[05:20] Aisha: back to procurement flow — once legal signs off on DPA redlines, procurement will run a final fee approval. we need an estimate of first-year TCO for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[05:33] Diego: i'll build a pilot cost estimate: per-token hosted baseline, dedicated reserved for steady traffic, and private license + infra ops for on-prem. i'll include unit cost assumptions.
[05:44] Jamal: for the POC, we want to test both throughput (tokens/sec) and failover behavior — if a model variant is unavailable, what's the policy?
[05:54] Diego: we have routing fallbacks: policy-based routing can route to cheaper/compatible variants; in Dedicated we can enable auto-fallback to hosted as a failover with explicit consent. we'll document tradeoffs for consistency vs cost.
[06:08] Priya: any concerns about export controls or data residency? our legal flagged EU customer data that must stay in eu region.
[06:16] Maya: we have region pinning and data residency controls—production can be pinned to eu-west to comply. note that some hardware variants reside only in certain regions; we'll flag those constraints.
[06:29] Aisha: okay, i think we've covered most. next steps recap?
[06:34] Maya: i'll share SOC2/ISO + data flow doc; diego will share pilot config and cost; aisha will return DPA redlines; liam/jamal will prepare KMS questions. can we tentatively schedule the KMS deep dive for 2025-04-28?
[06:50] Liam: yes that works.
[06:52] Aisha: 2025-04-21 is our internal DPA review cutoff so we'll aim to send redlines then.
[06:59] Maya: perfect. anything else?
[07:02] Jamal: small note — can the audit logs be anonymized for certain fields? we sometimes need masked PII in logs.
[07:09] Diego: we support log redaction rules and field masking; we'll include options in the audit export doc.
[07:18] Priya: also, contractually we'll want to confirm subprocessor list and 30-day notice for new subprocessors.
[07:25] Maya: understood — i'll include subprocessors table.
[07:29] Aisha: thanks all, we'll move quickly on the DPA side.
[07:33] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and i'll send calendar invites for the KMS deep dive.
[57:45] End of recording
